newsitem.title: INDIA: India's panel chief argues for disinvestment fund.
newsitem.headline: India's panel chief argues for disinvestment fund.

text.p: India should keep money raised through sales of shares in state-owned firms separate and not use it to help cover the budget deficit, G.V. Ramakrishna, chairman of India's Disinvestment Commission said in a newspaper interview on Friday.

The head of the panel overseeing India's partial privatisation programme spelled out reasons for recommending the creation of a Disinvestment Fund in an interview published by the Business Standard daily.

The 1997/98 budget (April-March) proposed raising 48 billion rupees ($1.34 billion) for sales of shares in state-run companies, despite expecting to raise less than one-tenth of its 50 billion rupee target for current 1996/97 fiscal year.

"If disinvestment proceeds are used in a fungible manner (to fund the budget deficit) it will obfuscate the need for fiscal discipline and conventional measures to minimise the revenue deficit like improving the tax effort and cutting down subsidies," he said.

"This (the fund) will add to the transparency and once the public sector lobby sees that there is a fund dedicated to its better health , the disinvestment process will become more acceptable," he said.
He listed a number of ways in the fund could be utilised, including using it to make provisions for loss-making units.
"Capital receipts from sale are one-time whereas incurring cash losses is usually recurring. So a balancing out over several years is necessary," Ramakrishna said.
Use of the proceeds for restructuring and rejuvenation will prevent a future drain on resources by turning units around, he said.

"Ideally after a few years, when loss making units are taken care of one way or another, the positive accruals in the fund can be used to retire public debt and bring long term benefit to the fiscal process by reducing the interest burden," he said.
The panel has also recommended that the proposed fund should be merged with the National Renewal Fund, from which voluntary retirement payments are made.

Ramakrishna also said there was support within government to grant Public Sector Units more autonomy. He also said many PSU unions want better managed companies with autonomous boards, which will prevent companies from sliding and protect jobs.
He said the speed of the disinvestment process depended on how fast the government acted on the panel's recommendations.

He said the government has alreaady accepted specific proposals for disinvestment in India Tourism Development Corp (ITDC), Modern Food Industries (india) Ltd and Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL), and said it will hand the panel another batch of PSUs for advice on their disinvestment.
